Title: Donation receipt references carry 30 bits of entropy on an endpoint that is deliberately not caller-scoped and is unthrottled

The two requirements never apply to one receipt: a reference read aloud to support belongs to a gift support can identify which caller-scoping now protects outright so its entropy is irrelevant and it stays at six characters. A reference that must be guess-proof belongs to a gift nobody owns where there is no account for support to tie it to at all. The ReceiptReference column is already 256 wide and its unique index covers the whole string so a longer anonymous form needed no schema change. Measured: 1 donation exists in the production database and it has an owner so 0 pre-existing ownerless receipts carry the old 30 bits and the forward-only generator leaves no residue. Two register claims did not survive checking. The endpoint is not unthrottled -- BSEC-002 gave it the Authenticated tier at 300 a minute which slows enumeration to about 2.5 days per address rather than preventing it. And remediation step 1 proposed issuing the high-entropy token with the receipt notification but DonationCompletedConsumer sends an anonymous donation no notification at all and says why: the contract carries no identifier to send it to. The read path is still load-bearing for a better reason that the register does not state: an anonymous gift completes asynchronously after its payment and appears in no history so this route is the only way its giver can learn the money arrived which is why the fix had to preserve it rather than scope it away. The handler comment asserting that the generator makes references unguessable was false and is replaced. The generator no longer carves its suffix out of a UUIDv7 byte layout nor takes a modulo that was unbiased only because 32 divides 256 -- both were true but untested and either would have cut the entropy silently. A refusal and a miss return one answer from one method so the endpoint is not an existence oracle. Both files restored byte-identically by hash. NOT done: the per-caller rate-limit dimension in criterion 2. The platform limiter partitions on address alone and changing that is a BSEC-002-wide decision which also loosens every other budget for one address holding several accounts so it does not belong in a Financial change. A refused or missed lookup now logs a warning naming the caller and never the reference because for an ownerless receipt the reference is the credential.
